newsitem.title: USA: FDA OK's first drug to protect against poison ivy.
newsitem.headline: FDA OK's first drug to protect against poison ivy.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration said Wednesday it had approved the first drug to protect people against poison ivy.

Available without prescription, the drug, bentoquatam 5 percent, is wrapped in a clay-like substance and applied to skin at least 15 minutes before possible exposure to poison ivy, oak and sumac, to provide a barrier that protects against or reduces the severity of the rash the plants cause, it said in a statement. It is not for use by people already affected.
Bentoquatam is made by Enviroderm of Louisville, Ky., under the name Ivy Block.
